verses.1: A psalm of David. I will sing to you, O LORD, of steadfast love and judgment. I will make music to you.
verses.2: I will consider the path of the blameless—when will you come to me? I will walk in my house with a wholehearted disposition.
verses.3: I will not set before my eyes anything that is worthless; I hate those who do wrong. Let them not cling to me.
verses.4: A crooked heart will turn away from me. I will not know evil.
verses.5: The one who slanders in secret, I will put to death. The proud of eye and wide in heart, I cannot eat with.
verses.6: My eyes are on those who are faithful in the land, to dwell with them; the one who walks in the blameless way—he will serve me.
verses.7: The one who makes himself arrogant in my house, who speaks lies, shall not remain before my eyes.
verses.8: At dawn I will destroy all the wicked of the land, to root out from the city of the LORD all who do evil.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "Let them not cling to me" reflects the idea of the Hebrew "lo yidbakkuni" which is a poetic way of saying the speaker will not allow them to stay close.
- v. 5: "I cannot eat with" renders the Hebrew "lo uchal" which implies refusal to accept or tolerate.
- v. 6: "he will serve me" reflects the Hebrew "hu yesharteni" with "yeshar" meaning to serve or support.
- v. 8: "root out" renders "lekhitkot" which is a reflexive form meaning to be cut off or eradicated.
raw:
[1] A psalm of David. I will sing to you, O LORD, of steadfast love and judgment. I will make music to you.

[2] I will consider the path of the blameless—when will you come to me? I will walk in my house with a wholehearted disposition.

[3] I will not set before my eyes anything that is worthless; I hate those who do wrong. Let them not cling to me.

[4] A crooked heart will turn away from me. I will not know evil.

[5] The one who slanders in secret, I will put to death. The proud of eye and wide in heart, I cannot eat with.

[6] My eyes are on those who are faithful in the land, to dwell with them; the one who walks in the blameless way—he will serve me.

[7] The one who makes himself arrogant in my house, who speaks lies, shall not remain before my eyes.

[8] At dawn I will destroy all the wicked of the land, to root out from the city of the LORD all who do evil.

---
Notes
- v. 3: "Let them not cling to me" reflects the idea of the Hebrew "lo yidbakkuni" which is a poetic way of saying the speaker will not allow them to stay close.
- v. 5: "I cannot eat with" renders the Hebrew "lo uchal" which implies refusal to accept or tolerate.
- v. 6: "he will serve me" reflects the Hebrew "hu yesharteni" with "yeshar" meaning to serve or support.
- v. 8: "root out" renders "lekhitkot" which is a reflexive form meaning to be cut off or eradicated.
